reason: While the passage (Exodus 12:31-39) emphasizes the Hebrews' instruction to worship/serve Yahweh (וּלְכוּ עִבְדוּ אֶת־ יְהוָה) and shows God's distinction between Israel and Egypt (יַפְלֶה יְהוָה בֵּין מִצְרַיִם וּבֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל), it does not explicitly assert that worship makes them a people. Rather, the text presupposes their existence as a distinct people (בְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל) and describes God's liberation and command to worship as consequences of divine choice, not as constitutive of their peoplehood. The text establishes that worship is central to their covenantal relationship with God following liberation, but the causal claim that worship MAKES them a people is not present in the passage.
